page: Microsoft Azure E48ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz, the processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations. The instance is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, and includes 2835 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in memory-intensive and data-processing tasks. The server achieves top-tier results in cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth at 3532.63 GB/sec, single-threaded gzip compression, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Database and key-value store performance is notable, with Redis SET operations reaching 76.28 million operations per second and static web serving throughput measured at 61.11 GB/sec. CPU performance is robust, scoring in the top 25% on Passmark CPU, extended instructions, and encryption tests, though standard stress-ng multi-core and single-core CPU benchmarks fall within the average range.

From a resource density perspective, the E48ds_v7 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads by bundling a substantial 384.0 GB RAM allocation with fast local storage, reducing the need to provision larger, more expensive compute tiers solely for memory capacity. However, hardware tradeoffs are present; while the processor's AMX instructions support strong prompt processing speeds for small and medium LLMs, text generation for large 70B models is weak, averaging 2.64 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. This server is best suited for memory-intensive databases, caching layers like Redis, large-scale data processing, and enterprise web serving.
